correctness.rationale: Correctness of the repaired files in repairs/3: expanding the normalized quotient near retention a=1, its positive-degree coefficient of index k is (1-a)(b_k-b_(k+1))+O((1-a)^2), with b_k=nu theta^k+(-1)^(k-1)r^k. This analytic expansion near zero also covers r>theta irrespective of the numerator zero elsewhere. For odd k the differences are positive; on the even subsequence r>theta must fail eventually, while r<=theta makes k=2 the strongest comparison, including ties when r=theta. When the differences d_k are nonnegative, they sum to b_1 and log H_a is the integral from a to 1 of sum_k d_k[(1-s+sz)^k-1] ds/s. Nonnegative binomial coefficients and total intensity bounded by b_1 log(1/a) prove sufficiency for all retentions and all indices. The strict inclusion in the classical ID region and overdispersion 15/16 at (nu,theta,p)=(1,1/2,1/4) were verified exactly. The repaired standard-library script passed with python3 -I /workspace/repairs/3/verify.py, including equality and a late-index failure with d_2>0. The frozen checker was read, not executed. The removed log-concavity classification was not rejected as false: the NB ratio gives the leading second log difference (1-nu)/k² below one, and the Bernoulli correction is the log of a linear-over-linear factor with second difference O(k^-3). In the frozen asymptotic display the constant in log f_k is real, not necessarily positive; this immaterial adjective is absent from the repair.

value.rationale: For a natural published count family used at many dispersion levels, the repaired claim provides a usable complete all-retention feasibility criterion that is strictly stronger than additive divisibility, including for overdispersed counts. It proves when an independent innovation exists, not just when a few coefficients pass; sufficiently late obstructions can arise when the odds exceed the NB parameter. The removed log-concavity result contributes no value to this revised claim.
